Snowball Edge supports S3-compatible storage and can run AWS Lambda functions and EC2 instances, making it suitable for edge computing tasks. It is available in different configurations, including storage and compute optimized options, to meet various workload requirements.

AWS Snowcone is a compact, rugged edge computing and data transfer device that enables collecting, processing, and transferring data to AWS from disconnected environments. Weighing under 5 lbs, Snowcone has 2 CPUs, 4 GB RAM, and 8-14 TB storage for running applications and migrating data to AWS offline by shipping the device or online using AWS DataSync. It's designed for harsh environments lacking space, power, or cooling common in data centers.

AWS Snowmobile was a data transfer service that used a 45-foot, ruggedized shipping container mounted on a semi-truck to physically move up to 100PB of data to AWS data centers. It was designed for exabyte-scale data migration, transferring data at 1Tbps across multiple 40Gbps connections. Snowmobile provided secure data transport with encryption, GPS tracking, and optional security escorts. However, AWS has retired the service as of 2024, citing more cost-effective and efficient data migration options like AWS DataSync and Snowball Edge devices.

AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage service that provides on-premises access to virtually unlimited cloud storage. It allows businesses to integrate their existing applications with AWS storage solutions without significant changes. Storage Gateway supports various protocols like iSCSI, SMB, and NFS, enabling low-latency access to frequently used data through local caching. It offers four gateway types: File Gateway, Volume Gateway, Tape Gateway, and FSx Gateway, optimizing data transfer and management between on-premises environments and AWS cloud services.
On-Premises Virtual Machines: VMware ESXi: You can run the Storage Gateway as a VM on VMware ESXi (versions 7.0 or 8.0). Microsoft Hyper-V: It can also be deployed as a VM on Microsoft Hyper-V (versions 2012 R2, 2016, 2019, or 2022). Linux KVM: Supported on various Linux distributions, including CentOS/RHEL and Ubuntu.
AWS Cloud: Amazon EC2 Instances: You can deploy Storage Gateway as an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) on EC2. This is suitable for all types of gateways (File, Volume, and Tape Gateways) but with specific instance type recommendations based on the gateway type.
Physical Hardware Appliance: For locations with limited virtual machine infrastructure, a dedicated hardware appliance is available.

AWS IoT 1-Click is a service that simplifies the management and deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, enabling users to easily trigger actions in the cloud without the need for complex configurations or custom firmware. It is particularly designed for basic devices that can initiate specific actions, such as sending notifications or triggering AWS Lambda functions.

AWS CloudHSM is a fully managed hardware security module (HSM) service that provides secure key storage and cryptographic operations in the AWS cloud. It allows organizations to manage their cryptographic keys with high security, ensuring compliance with stringent regulatory standards.

Fortinet FortiAnalyzer is a centralized security analytics and log management platform that aggregates, normalizes, and enriches data from Fortinet and third-party devices. It provides unified visibility, advanced threat detection, compliance reporting, and automation for security operations. With built-in SIEM, SOAR capabilities, and AI-powered analytics, FortiAnalyzer helps organizations streamline investigations, accelerate incident response, and improve operational efficiency across on-premises and cloud environments.

Fortinet FortiGate is a next-generation firewall that provides advanced network security features like intrusion prevention, web filtering, and VPN support to protect against cyber threats across organizations of all sizes.

Fortinet FortiManager is a centralized management platform that allows organizations to efficiently configure, monitor, and manage multiple Fortinet security devices and policies from a single, unified interface. This streamlines device provisioning, policy updates, and network security operations across large or distributed environments.

VMware ESXi is a bare-metal (type-1) hypervisor that installs directly on physical servers, allowing multiple virtual machines—each with its own operating system and applications—to run securely and efficiently on the same hardware. With a lightweight architecture based on the VMkernel, ESXi abstracts and allocates server resources such as CPU, memory, and storage to virtual machines, enabling high performance, scalability, and simplified management without the need for a separate underlying operating system. It is a foundational component of VMware’s vSphere suite, widely used in enterprise and data center virtualization.

VMware vCenter Server is a centralized management platform for VMware vSphere environments, enabling administrators to configure, monitor, and control multiple ESXi hosts and virtual machines from a single interface. It streamlines operations such as resource provisioning, performance monitoring, automation, user privilege management, and advanced features like high availability, vMotion, and distributed resource scheduling. Delivered as a prepackaged virtual appliance, vCenter offers scalability, proactive management, and unified visibility across on-premises and hybrid cloud deployments.

VMware vSphere is a virtualization platform that enables organizations to run and manage multiple virtual machines on physical servers using the ESXi hypervisor and vCenter Server for centralized management. It offers features like high availability, efficient resource allocation, and scalability, making it ideal for modern data centers and private cloud environments.

A VMware virtual machine is a software-based computer that runs its own operating system and applications, using VMware's virtualization technology. It operates independently of other VMs on the same physical host, with resources managed by a hypervisor.

AWS VPC Carrier Gateway is a service that enables the establishment of direct, private connections between a customer's on-premises network and their AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). It simplifies network management by providing a single gateway that supports multiple AWS Regions, eliminating the need for separate VPN connections for each region. This service enhances security through private connections, ensures high bandwidth for data transfer, and utilizes Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) for dynamic routing, optimizing traffic paths and improving performance.

AWS VPC Customer Gateway is a physical device or software application located in your on-premises network that provides information to AWS about your VPN connection. It represents the customer endpoint of an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The Customer Gateway can be a router, firewall, or Linux server that supports IPsec VPNs. When setting up a VPN connection, you create a Customer Gateway resource in AWS that specifies the device's public IP address or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a private certificate. This allows AWS to establish the VPN tunnels to your on-premises network.

AWS VPC Internet Gateway is a horizontally scaled, redundant, and highly available component that enables communication between resources in your VPC and the internet. It supports IPv4 and IPv6 traffic. An internet gateway allows resources in your public subnets (like EC2 instances) to connect to the internet if they have a public IP address. It also enables resources on the internet to initiate a connection to resources in your VPC using their public IP address. An internet gateway provides a target in your VPC route tables for internet-routable traffic and performs network address translation (NAT) for IPv4 communication.

An AWS VPC NAT Gateway is a managed Network Address Translation service that allows instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound connections to the internet while keeping their private IP addresses hidden. It enables these instances to access external services for updates or downloads without exposing them to incoming traffic from the internet. NAT Gateways are created in public subnets and require an Elastic IP for internet access, ensuring secure and efficient communication for private resources within a VPC.

AWS Transit Gateway is a network service that acts as a central hub to interconnect multiple Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) and on-premises networks within AWS. It simplifies network architecture by allowing all traffic between VPCs and external networks to be routed through a single gateway, instead of requiring complex peering connections. The service supports dynamic routing and can handle high volumes of traffic, enhancing scalability and security by ensuring that data does not traverse the public internet.

AWS VPC VPN Gateway, specifically known as a Virtual Private Gateway (VGW), is a component that enables secure communication between your Amazon VPC and your on-premises network over an IPsec VPN connection. It acts as the VPN concentrator on the AWS side of the connection, allowing you to establish a site-to-site VPN. The VGW provides two VPN tunnels for redundancy and automatic failover, ensuring a reliable connection for data transmission between your VPC and external networks.

AWS CloudFormation is a service that enables users to define and provision AWS infrastructure as code using templates. These templates, written in JSON or YAML, describe the desired resources and their configurations, such as EC2 instances, S3 buckets, and VPCs. CloudFormation automates the deployment process, ensuring resources are created in the correct order and managing dependencies. This approach allows for consistent, repeatable infrastructure setups across different environments and accounts, enhancing efficiency and reducing manual errors.

AWS OpsWorks is a configuration management service that automates application deployment and operation using Chef or Puppet. It organizes apps into layers, applies configurations automatically, and supports EC2 instances and on-premises servers. OpsWorks provides managed Chef and Puppet servers, allowing you to define infrastructure as code, automate tasks, and manage the full application lifecycle. It integrates with CloudWatch for monitoring and CloudTrail for logging, simplifying operations. OpsWorks offers flexibility, scalability, and easy orchestration for deploying and managing applications in the cloud.

AWS Backup is a fully managed service designed to centralize and automate data protection across various AWS services and on-premises environments. It allows users to create backup policies, known as backup plans, to define how frequently to back up data and how long to retain it. AWS Backup supports multiple resource types, including Amazon EC2, RDS, DynamoDB, and EBS, simplifying backup management and compliance. It also features monitoring, auditing, and cross-region backup capabilities for enhanced security and recovery options.

AWS AppFlow is a fully managed integration service that facilitates secure data transfer between Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) applications and AWS services. It supports popular SaaS platforms like Salesforce, SAP, and Zendesk, allowing users to automate bi-directional data flows with minimal effort. AppFlow offers features such as data transformation, scheduling, and event-driven triggers, enabling seamless integration without extensive coding. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, ensuring security throughout the process, making it ideal for enterprise-scale data management.

AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS) is a service that enables fast and reliable recovery of on-premises and cloud-based applications, minimizing downtime and data loss. It allows users to replicate applications to AWS, facilitating quick recovery within minutes to their most recent state or a previous point in time. AWS DRS automates the recovery process, supports non-disruptive testing, and helps maintain compliance by enabling recovery across different AWS regions or from on-premises to AWS.

AWS Auto Scaling (management node) refers to the automated management of Amazon EC2 instances within a managed node group in Amazon EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service). It simplifies the lifecycle of nodes by automatically provisioning, updating, and terminating EC2 instances based on demand. Each managed node is part of an EC2 Auto Scaling group, ensuring high availability and efficient resource utilization. The management node also integrates with the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler, enabling dynamic scaling based on workload requirements, thus optimizing performance and cost without manual intervention.

An AWS Auto Scaling Group (ASG) is a logical collection of Amazon EC2 instances that enables automatic scaling and management of those instances based on demand. It ensures that the desired number of instances are running by automatically launching or terminating instances according to defined policies. ASGs maintain a minimum and maximum instance count, perform health checks, and can integrate with Elastic Load Balancing to distribute traffic. This functionality helps optimize performance and cost by dynamically adjusting resources to match application load.

AWS Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) is a high-performance network interface for Amazon EC2 instances that enables enhanced networking capabilities. ENA provides up to 20 Gbps of bandwidth, low latency, high packet per second performance, and reduced CPU utilization compared to traditional network interfaces. It supports features like checksum offload, TCP segmentation offload, and receive-side scaling to optimize network performance. ENA is designed to scale with increasing vCPU counts and network bandwidth, allowing customers to take advantage of future improvements without changing drivers or configurations.

An AWS Elastic Network Interface (ENI) is a virtual network interface that enables communication between Amazon EC2 instances and the network within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Each ENI can have one primary private IPv4 address, multiple secondary private IPv4 addresses, and support for Elastic IP addresses. ENIs allow for flexible attachment and detachment from instances, facilitating dynamic network management. They enhance security by integrating with security groups and network access control lists, enabling granular control over inbound and outbound traffic.

AWS Perimeter Zone is a security architecture that acts as a boundary for applications connecting to the internet, often referred to as a Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). It exposes applications and services to external users while adding an additional layer of security. This zone helps control incoming and outgoing traffic from a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and is typically protected by firewalls and other security measures. By isolating internet-facing applications, AWS Perimeter Zones enhance overall network security and manage data flows effectively.

AWS Local Zones are an extension of AWS infrastructure that brings select services closer to large population centers, enabling low-latency access for applications. Designed for latency-sensitive workloads, Local Zones allow users to deploy resources like Amazon EC2 and RDS in geographic proximity to end-users, providing single-digit millisecond latency. Each Local Zone operates as a subnet within a parent AWS Region, facilitating seamless integration with existing AWS services while maintaining high performance and responsiveness for real-time applications.

AWS Region is a distinct geographic area that contains multiple, isolated locations known as Availability Zones (AZs). Each region is designed to be independent, providing fault tolerance and stability, ensuring that resources in one region are not affected by issues in another. AWS Regions enable users to deploy applications closer to their end-users, improving latency and compliance with data residency requirements. Each region offers a variety of services, allowing for flexibility in resource management and application deployment across the AWS global infrastructure.

AWS Availability Zones (AZs) are isolated locations within an AWS Region, designed to provide high availability and fault tolerance for applications. Each AZ consists of one or more discrete data centers, equipped with independent power, cooling, and networking. This physical separation minimizes the risk of simultaneous failures. AZs are interconnected through low-latency links, allowing for seamless data replication and load balancing. By distributing resources across multiple AZs, users can enhance application resilience and maintain uptime even during localized disruptions.

The Attachment capability is the default TOSCA type for defining an attachment capability of a (logical) infrastructure device node (e.g., BlockStorage node).
The Compute capability, when included on a Node Type or Template definition, indicates that the node can provide hosting on a named compute resource.
The Container capability, when included on a Node Type or Template definition, indicates that the node can act as a container for (or a host for) one or more other declared Node Types.
The Endpoint.Admin capability is the default TOSCA type for defining a specialized administrator endpoint capability
The Node capability indicates the base capabilities of a TOSCA Node Type.
The OperatingSystem capability is the default TOSCA type for expressing an Operating System capability for a node.
The OperatingSystem capability is the default TOSCA type for expressing a scalability capability for a node.
A node type that includes the Bindable capability indicates that it can be bound to a logical network association via a network port.
The Credential type describes authorization credentials used to access network-accessible resources
The Network type describes logical network information.
The PortInfo type describes network port information.
The PortSpec type is used when describing port specifications for a network connection.
The Standard lifecycle interface defines the essential normative operations that TOSCA nodes may support.
The Configure lifecycle interface defines the essential normative operations that TOSCA relationships may support.
The TOSCA Node Type all other TOSCA base Node Types derive from.
The TOSCA SoftwareComponent node represents a generic software component that can be managed and run by a TOSCA compute node.
The AttachesTo type represents an attachment relationship between two nodes (e.g. for attaching a storage node to a Compute node).
The DependsOn type represents a general dependency relationship between two nodes.
The HostedOn type represents a hosting relationship between two nodes.
